rates.method_note: Department of Finance, Rate Poundages: domestic district and regional rates for Belfast, in £ per £1 of capital value; each district rate matches the Department for Communities' rate statistics.

example_value.label: the average capital value of a home in Northern Ireland
example_value.method_note: Department of Finance, 12 February 2026, note 2: the average capital value in the Domestic Valuation List. There is no official average for Belfast.

amount_raised.method_note: Department for Communities, District Council Rate Statistics 2026/2027, Table 1 (page 1): total amount to be raised, and the balance applied from reserves (none).

funding.label: District rates (homes and businesses)
funding.official_term: Estimated amount to be raised via district rates (rateable)
funding.desc: The council's part of every rates bill, paid by homes and businesses alike. The regional rate on the same bill goes to the Executive, not the council
funding.method_note: Department for Communities, District Council Rate Statistics 2026/2027, Table 2 (page 2): estimated amount to be raised via district rates.

funding.label: De-rating grant
funding.desc: Paid by the Executive to make up the rates that some property, such as factories, is let off
funding.method_note: Department for Communities, District Council Rate Statistics 2026/2027, Table 2 (page 2): estimated de-rating grant.

services.label: Bins, streets, parks, leisure and communities
services.official_term: People and Communities Committee cash limit
services.desc: Bin collections and recycling, street cleaning, parks and open spaces, leisure centres, community services and environmental health
services.method_note: Belfast City Council, Strategic Policy and Resources Committee, 13 February 2026, resolution 2: the People and Communities Committee's cash limit for 2026-27 (page 3).

services.label: Running the council, and city funds
services.official_term: Strategic Policy and Resources Committee cash limit
services.desc: The council's own finance, staff, property and legal services, with £0.9m for the Belfast Investment Fund and £3.0m towards the Belfast Region City Deal
services.method_note: Belfast City Council, Strategic Policy and Resources Committee, 13 February 2026, resolution 2: the Strategic Policy and Resources Committee's cash limit, including £900,000 for the Belfast Investment Fund and £3,000,000 for City Deal for 2026-27 (page 3).

services.label: Paying for past building projects
services.desc: Repaying the loans and setting aside money for buildings, parks and other long-term projects
services.method_note: Belfast City Council, Strategic Policy and Resources Committee, 13 February 2026, resolution 2: the Capital Financing Budget for 2026-27 (page 3).

services.label: Jobs, tourism, culture and regeneration
services.official_term: City Growth and Regeneration Committee cash limit
services.desc: Help for businesses and jobs, tourism, events, culture and the arts, markets and regenerating the city centre
services.method_note: Belfast City Council, Strategic Policy and Resources Committee, 13 February 2026, resolution 2: the City Growth and Regeneration Committee's cash limit for 2026-27 (page 3).

services.label: Growth fund
services.desc: Set aside for new spending this year. The minutes give it only as £4.2m, so this is what the total leaves once the other lines are taken off
services.method_note: The amount to be raised (Department for Communities, Table 1) less the four committees' cash limits and the capital financing budget; the minutes say "A growth fund of 4.2m" (page 3).

services.label: Planning
services.desc: Deciding planning applications and preparing the city's plan for how land is used
services.method_note: Belfast City Council, Strategic Policy and Resources Committee, 13 February 2026, resolution 2: the Planning Committee's cash limit for 2026-27 (page 3).
